criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test -p athena-cli drain`. A new drain test queues an item on a line with a pause file, then a second ordinary item. It asserts that the paused item is not read (zero read calls for it), that exactly one printed line names the line and how to lift the pause, that no failure is counted and the stop is not `repeated-failure`, and that the next item runs and lands.
criteria.evidence: `drain_passes_over_an_item_on_a_paused_line_unread_with_one_line_and_runs_the_next_item` passed. It asserts the log is exactly [read b, run b, land b, rate], so a is never read; Stop::QueueEmpty; failed_item None; landed 1; exactly one recorded Ui line naming the line and the lift text, printed before any run; and zero such lines in the rendered report. The RealSteps test `drain_real_steps_pass_over_the_item_of_a_line_that_is_still_paused_without_reading_it` also passed: no read or run happened (repository head unchanged), one passed-over line, and the stop is not RepeatedFailure.

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test -p athena-cli drain`. A new drain test queues the same paused-line item three times, followed by an ordinary item. It asserts that the drain does not stop on repeated failure and that the ordinary item still runs.
criteria.evidence: `drain_does_not_stop_on_repeated_failure_for_items_of_a_paused_line_and_works_the_next_item` passed (a1, a2 and a3 paused, a2 depending on a1, then c). The log is [read c, run c, land c, rate], Stop::QueueEmpty, failed_item None, and each paused item has exactly one passed-over line. The mid-run case `..._paused_by_its_own_failed_attempt_without_a_second_attempt` also passed.

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test -p athena-cli plan`. A new plan test with a pause file for a line shows its queued item listed as held, with the pause reason and lift instruction from `pause_refusal`. The same test shows a queued item on an unpaused line is not listed as held.
criteria.evidence: `plan_lists_an_item_on_a_paused_line_as_held_with_the_pause_reason_and_not_read` passed. a is held with the exact reason and empty `missing`; its dependent c is held; b is not held; plan.order is [b]; the rendered text has `held        a · make it better: <reason>` and no `held        b`; nothing is read. The reason is fake-Steps text shaped like `pause_refusal`'s output. A separate RealSteps test asserts that `steps.paused` returns `athena.pause_refusal(&mark)`, so the real reason is covered in two pieces.

criteria.criterion: CHANGELOG.md has an entry that says drain passes over items on a paused line, prints one line, does not count them as failures, and plan lists them as held.
criteria.evidence: The diff adds a bullet under Unreleased/Fixed. criteria.criterion: A stale pause (one `line_pause` no longer reports) does not hold an item. Pass-over uses `Athena::line_pause`, not just the existence of the pause file, as shown by the diff in the real Steps implementation.
criteria.evidence: In the diff, `RealSteps::paused` calls `self.athena.line_pause(&records, job)` and then `pause_refusal(&mark)`. It never checks only whether the file exists. In scope_guard.rs, `line_pause` (line 782) recomputes the line's level and returns a mark only when the level is Pause. The test `drain_real_steps_do_not_hold_an_item_for_a_stored_pause_that_no_longer_holds` writes a stale pause file on a flagged line and asserts that `steps.paused` is empty and that the plan holds nothing as paused. It passed.

findings.summary: No single test runs `drain::plan` through RealSteps with a real pause and checks the held reason against `pause_refusal`.
findings.evidence: The planned demonstration for criterion 3 described a RealSteps plan test. The real-pause RealSteps test runs `drain::drain` and checks `steps.paused(...) == pause_refusal(&mark)`; the plan test uses the fake Stub. Together they cover the path, but not in one test.

findings.summary: `RealSteps::paused` loads the records again on every attempt, including for items on lines that are not paused.
findings.evidence: `Drain::attempts` calls `steps.paused(&[item.job])` before every read or run, and `RealSteps::paused` calls `self.records()` each time. This is correct, but it repeats work that could be shared with the read.

summary: The change does what the request asks. `athena drain` now asks once, through a new `Steps::paused` method and before it reads anything, which queued items are on a paused line. It does not read those items, holds back the items that depend on them, prints one `plan  <item> passed over: <pause_refusal text>` line for each before any other item runs, and leaves them out of the failure count. A new `ItemEnd::Paused` check before each attempt covers a line that an item's own failed first attempt has just paused. `athena plan` lists these items as `held` with the same reason. The real Steps implementation uses `Athena::line_pause` and `pause_refusal`, so a stale pause file holds nothing. I ran `cargo test -p athena-cli drain` and `cargo test -p athena-cli --test drain plan` in the snapshot, and all the new tests passed. The recorded CI results show fmt, clippy and the full test suite passing. Only CHANGELOG.md, drain.rs and tests/drain.rs changed, all within the deliverables; reading.rs and docs/decisions.md are untouched. One minor gap: the plan test that checks the `pause_refusal` reason uses the fake Steps with text copied from `pause_refusal`. The real path is covered in two pieces (`RealSteps::paused` returns `pause_refusal` text, and the fake-Steps plan test shows that text listed as held), but no single test runs it end to end.
